subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following is an energy store rather than a transfer pathway?
questions.explain: Energy is held in stores such as kinetic, chemical and gravitational, whereas heating, radiation and working are pathways that transfer energy between stores.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of work done?
questions.explain: Work done is a form of energy transfer and so is measured in joules (J).

questions.q: Which statement best describes the principle of conservation of energy?
options: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred from one store to another
Energy is always increased when a machine does work
Energy is destroyed when it is dissipated to the surroundings
Energy can be created if enough force is applied
questions.explain: The total energy of a closed system stays constant; energy is only transferred between stores, never created or destroyed.

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy resource?
questions.explain: Wind is renewable because it is naturally replenished and will not run out, unlike fossil fuels or nuclear fuel.

questions.q: Which of these is a non-renewable energy resource?
questions.explain: Coal is a fossil fuel that forms over millions of years and is used far faster than it is replaced, making it non-renewable.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.explain: Power is the rate of energy transfer and is measured in watts (W), where one watt equals one joule per second.

questions.q: Which equation correctly gives the work done by a force?
options: Work done = force × distance moved in the direction of the force
questions.explain: Work done (J) = force (N) × distance moved in the direction of the force (m).

questions.q: In a typical power station, the turbine is used to turn a device that produces electricity. What is this device called?
questions.explain: A turbine turns the generator, which converts kinetic energy into electrical energy for the National Grid.

questions.q: When a moving car brakes and slows to a stop, where is most of its kinetic energy transferred?
options: To the thermal store of the brakes and surroundings
To the chemical store of the fuel
To the gravitational store of the car
To the elastic store of the tyres
questions.explain: Friction in the brakes transfers the car's kinetic energy to the thermal store of the brakes and surrounding air by heating.

questions.q: What is meant when we say energy has been 'dissipated'?
options: It has been spread out to the surroundings and become less useful
It has been stored so it can be reused later
It has been created by a machine doing work
questions.explain: Dissipated energy is transferred to the surroundings, usually as thermal energy, and becomes spread out and no longer useful.

questions.q: On a Sankey diagram for an energy transfer, what does the width of an arrow represent?
options: The speed of the energy transfer
questions.explain: In a Sankey diagram the width of each arrow is drawn in proportion to the amount of energy it represents.

questions.q: Why can no real machine ever be 100% efficient?
options: Some of the input energy is always dissipated as wasted energy
Energy is destroyed inside the machine
The useful output energy is always greater than the input
questions.explain: Some input energy is always transferred to unwanted stores, usually thermal, so the useful output is always less than the total input.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes a renewable energy resource?
options: It is replenished naturally and will not run out
It releases no energy when used
It can only be used once before it is destroyed
It always produces more energy than is put in
questions.explain: A renewable resource is one that is replenished at least as fast as it is used, so it will not be exhausted.

questions.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of generating electricity using wind turbines?
options: They only generate electricity when it is windy, so output is unreliable
They release large amounts of carbon dioxide
They use up fossil fuels quickly
questions.explain: Wind power is intermittent because turbines cannot generate a steady output when there is little or no wind.

questions.q: As an object falls freely towards the ground, which energy transfer takes place?
questions.explain: As the object falls it loses height and gravitational potential energy, which is transferred to its kinetic store as it speeds up.

questions.q: Which quantity does power measure?
options: The rate at which energy is transferred
The total energy stored in an object
The force needed to move an object
questions.explain: Power is the amount of energy transferred, or work done, per unit time.

questions.q: A force of 30 N pushes a box 4 m in the direction of the force. How much work is done?
questions.explain: Work done = force × distance = 30 N × 4 m = 120 J.

questions.q: A motor transfers 600 J of energy in 30 s. What is its power output?
questions.explain: Power = energy transferred ÷ time = 600 J ÷ 30 s = 20 W.

questions.q: A mass of 5 kg is lifted 2 m at a steady speed. Taking g = 10 N/kg, how much gravitational potential energy does it gain?
questions.explain: Change in GPE = m × g × Δh = 5 kg × 10 N/kg × 2 m = 100 J.

questions.q: A device is supplied with 500 J of energy and usefully transfers 150 J. What is its efficiency?
questions.explain: Efficiency = useful energy output ÷ total energy input = 150 J ÷ 500 J = 0.30, which is 30%.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics (4PH1) specification; Energy Resources & Energy Transfers
